text:
Daybreak comes raining. Well combed,

the morning drips its fine hair.

Melancholy is tied up;

and in badly asphalted oxident of Hindu furniture,

fate turns, barely settles.


Skies of heartbroken puna

from great love, the platinum skies, grim

with impossible.


The flock ruminates and underlines itself

with an Andean neigh.


I remember myself. But enough

are the antlers of the wind, the rudders still until

becoming one,

and the cricket of tedium and the hunchback's unbreakable elbow.


Enough the morning of free loose manes

of precious pitch, mountain-born,

when I go out and look for eleven

and they are only twelve unhours.

translation.title: Trilce: Poem LXIII - Daybreak Comes Raining. Well Combed
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves 'oxident' and 'unhours' to keep the poem's invented temporal/weather language.
